posts.title: Reliability at the core: five ground rules for building an agent loop
posts.description: Five ground rules for building an AI agent loop with reliability at its core, learned building Kept: lay down the state machine before the code, separate the loop runner from the host, turn errors into outcomes, keep the history atomic, and assert every transition three ways.

posts.title: Putting the trace before the loop
posts.description: Observability is the bedrock of reliability, so I designed and implemented the full tracing layer for an AI agent before writing a single line of the agent loop. Three benefits, two drawbacks, and the span tree that turned out to be the loop's control flow.

posts.title: Did it check, or did it guess? Testing a tool whose output is written by an LLM
posts.description: My first AI tool worked, or at least the output looked right when I ran it. Then I pictured a client asking what makes it trustworthy: did it check, or did it guess? This is how I built a real answer, and how designing the output for testing made the tool harder to lie with.
